extracted.intended_audience: general newspaper readers / policymakers interested in international affairs
extracted.subtask_description: News reporting covering international events, diplomatic proposals, post-war refugee policy, military operations, labor disputes, and reconstruction efforts. The page collects multiple Associated Press dispatches and summaries for a general readership.

rubrics_metrics.name: U.S. immigration admission standards for displaced persons
rubrics_metrics.description: “There is no proposal to waive or lower our present prescribed standards for testing the fitness of immigrants ... These laws provide adequate guaranties against the entry of those who are criminals or subversives, those likely to become public charges and those who are otherwise undesirable.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: President Truman urged Congress to admit a substantial number of Europe’s displaced persons but explicitly said the present immigration statutes and testing of fitness should be retained; any special legislation should not lower the existing standards or waive requirements (e.g., criminality, subversive tendencies, likelihood of becoming a public charge).

rubrics_metrics.name: Non‑refoulement criterion for displaced persons
rubrics_metrics.description: “These people ... are unwilling by reason of political opinion and fear of persecution to return to the areas where they once had homes.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The President and dispatches argue the United States should not support returning displaced persons to their former homes by force where it is evident their unwillingness to return is based on political opinion or fear of persecution; this is presented as a fundamental humanitarian constraint on repatriation policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope limitation for emergency resettlement legislation
rubrics_metrics.description: “Special legislation limited to this particular emergency will therefore be necessary.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Truman frames any new admission measure as a narrowly tailored emergency program addressing a specific group of war victims in Allied occupation hands, not as a general overhaul of immigration policy; he did not specify numeric quotas in the message.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adequate basic training before front‑line deployment
rubrics_metrics.description: “Any attempt to rush recruits through a basic training program in a few weeks would amount to mass suicide as the Szepingkai battle proved.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reporting emphasizes that sending inadequately trained recruits (e.g., with only one week of training) into combat produces catastrophic losses; training duration and thoroughness are presented as safety and effectiveness criteria for mobilization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Labor standard wage demand (Japan unions)
rubrics_metrics.description: “Union officials ... advocating a standard wage of 2,600 yen ($52) monthly ... expressed dissatisfaction with the 1,800 yen ($36) average wage established by Premier Tetsu Katayama’s cabinet.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Japanese union leaders judged the government’s wage‑price program inadequate to guarantee a minimum standard of living and proposed a specific standard wage (2,600 yen) as the criterion for acceptable policy; the article notes government measures (price adjustments) and their limited expected impact relative to black‑market rates.

rubrics_metrics.name: UNRRA reconstruction performance target for railway repair
rubrics_metrics.description: “The 90-mile stretch of railway is to be repaired and in operating condition again in a week, officials said.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: UNRRA’s rehabilitation plan includes concrete performance expectations (repair and restoration of specific railway sections within a stated timeframe) and hardware deliveries (locomotives from abroad) as measures of program progress and success.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principles for a doctrine of internal and external peace (Argentina proposal)
rubrics_metrics.description: Argentina proposed a three‑point plan urging: (1) realization that only through peace can human happiness be attained; (2) acceptance that tranquillity is based upon respect for human rights; (3) support for ideals of judicial equality, obligatory arbitration, and economic co‑operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The proposal is presented as a normative rubric for international behavior — criteria (respect for human rights, judicial equality, compulsory arbitration, economic cooperation) to be endorsed and promoted by nations (Western Hemisphere and the Holy See) as foundations of lasting peace.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for provincial autonomy under constitutional guarantees (Japan governors’ complaint)
rubrics_metrics.description: “The governors accused [the] national Government to cease interfering in the affairs of Japan’s 46 prefectures ... autonomy ... is guaranteed under the new constitution.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefectural governors present non‑interference by the national government and respect for constitutionally guaranteed provincial autonomy as standards of proper governance; this functions as a political/legal criterion for central–local relations.
